position: Aligning Departmental Resources with Leadership Priorities
proposal: The Mandate recommends a holistic review of hiring practices across all DOJ offices and components to ensure compliance with law and policy. It recommends assessing hiring committees for career positions so that hires rest on merit, aptitude and legal skill, and not on ideological association or on race, religion or sex.

significance.rationale: DOJ would review hiring practices and career hiring committees across its components to confirm hires rest on merit and comply with law.

status_summary: An Attorney General memorandum of 2025-02-05 stated that race- or sex-based preferences and diversity hiring targets have no place in Department materials, and required each component to review hiring, promotion and performance-evaluation policies, with attention to ending DEI references, in a report due 2025-03-15. It also required components to end DEI performance requirements for employees. The memorandum does not mention hiring committees, ideology or political affiliation, and no department-wide review of committee impartiality was found.

timeline.event: The Attorney General issued a memorandum on eliminating internal discriminatory practices, requiring component reviews of hiring, promotion and performance-evaluation policies by 2025-03-15.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General

title: Review DOJ hiring practices for impartiality and compliance with law
uncertainties: Only the memorandum was read as a primary source. A review search on the Honors Program and career hiring found reports of rescinded 2025 offers and a 2026 memorandum suspending a one-year experience requirement for new prosecutors (reported by The Harvard Crimson), neither of which is a review of hiring committees. The memorandum addresses DEI-related hiring, which overlaps only in part with the Mandate's concern about ideological hiring. Component reports under the memorandum were not found.
